deep.reconstruction: The page (folio 45r, rotated 90 degrees in the scan) is a pure table with no prose. It is divided into eight blocks, headed 24n+1, 24n+5, 24n+13, 24n+17 (left half of the sheet) and 24n+7, 24n+11, 24n+19, 24n+23 (right half). Each block has a row index (1..12 for the first four, 1..13 for the others) and, per row, an affine expression in n with rational coefficients plus up to four 'correction' columns headed by the letters a, b, c, d, with a dot marking an empty entry. A heavy horizontal rule separates the row-label column from the data. Typical entries: for 24n+1, row k has main term (k/2)n, with additive terms in a, c, d of size 1/4, 1/12, 1/6, 1/3 (for example row 1: n/2 + a/4 ... +c/12 + d/4; row 4: 2n ... -c/3; row 12: 6n). For 24n+5, the main terms run n/2, n, 3n/2, 2n, 5n/2+1/2, 3n+1/2, ... 6n+1, with a, b, d corrections of +-1/4 or +-1/2. For 24n+13 the constant parts grow as 0, 1/2, 1/2, 1, 1, 3/2, 3/2, 2, 2, 5/2, 5/2, 3, i.e. about half the row index over 2, plus a, b, d corrections. 24n+17: constants 0, 1/2, 1, 1, 3/2, 2, 2, 5/2, 3, 7/2, 7/2, 4. 24n+7, 24n+11, 24n+19, 24n+23 have the constant (non-n) part inside the main column, with growing constants (e.g. 24n+23: 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3, 7/2, 4, 9/2, 5, 11/2, i.e. a floor-type linear function of the row index) and a, b, c, d coefficients of size 1/12, 1/6, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2. Reading the structure: the row index k=1..12 (13) evidently labels a count or sum over a range of size about k*(p/24), where p=24n+r is a prime, so the main term is k*p/48-type linear (here (k/2)n + const), and the a,b,c,d columns are the bounded fluctuating terms depending on the residue of p (presumably a,b,c,d are parameters of a representation of p or of a character sum, such as p = a^2 + b^2-type data or the signs/values of quadratic, quartic, octic or 24th-order characters). Thus each block gives, for p in a fixed class mod 24, the number of something (residues, non-residues, or sums of residue indicators) in the k-th twelfth (or twenty-fourth) part of 1..p-1. This is in the style of Gauss's work on biquadratic residues, on the distribution of residues of order 8 / 12 / 24, or on cyclotomic numbers. The page is the end of a long computation: the previous page begins a Gaussian-integer computation (norm arithmetic with a+bi) and cyclic-index work (a^alpha = 1 mod p), so the table is likely a summary of distribution counts. I cannot identify from the page alone which quantity is counted or what a,b,c,d are; this is unclear. Sample checks: in every block the n-coefficient of row k is exactly k/2, giving 6n at row 12 (6n = (p-r)/4), consistent with a total count of about p/4 when the full range is taken, so the structure is self-consistent. The rows 12 of 24n+1, 24n+5, 24n+13, 24n+17 have no correction terms (dots) except constants, and row 12 of 24n+5 and 24n+13 are 6n+1 and 6n+3 which equal (p-5)/4+... : (24n+5)/4 = 6n+5/4, so 6n+1 = (p-1)/4 and 6n+3 for 24n+13 = (p-1)/4 = 6n+3 exactly; for 24n+17 row 12 is 6n+4 = (p-1)/4 = 6n+4 exactly; for 24n+1, 6n = (p-1)/4 exactly. All four checks agree: row 12 equals (p-1)/4. For 24n+7, 24n+11, 24n+19, 24n+23 row 12 constants are 3/2+a/2, 5/2+a/2, 9/2+a/2, 11/2+a/2; here (p-1)/4 would be 6n+3/2, 6n+5/2, 6n+9/2, 6n+11/2, matching the constants exactly with an extra a/2 term. So the final (row 12) entries are internally consistent with (p-1)/4 up to a correction, a good sign of correct copying. Entries in the first column of the 24n+5 and 24n+13 blocks interleave with a-column entries, and the transcription's column alignment is uncertain in places. I did not restate every entry.
